title: Apply the smaller halo exponents across a cell, under the downward reading (no new κ)
body:
## Question

#4439 left the exponents 12, 26, 28, 28 and 6 on the rounded block inside one cell. Do they survive on the banded reference, whose across-cell entries are the downward Gaussian entries rather than `ahat_j Ghat_(j-k)/ahat_k`?

## Lemma

Assume the ideal row and column off-sums are at most `1-1/(8p^2)`, each within-cell off-diagonal entry is at most the matching entry of `N` divided by `1-ε` with `ε≤1/(16p^2)`, and each across-cell entry lies in `[0, n]`. For an integer bandwidth `W≤p-1`, both gaps of `H` are at least `1/(16p^2-1)`. Hence `||H||_2<2` and `||H^{-1}||_2≤16p^2-1`.

The polynomial `P=p^{-12} sum_{j<p^{26}} Q^j H^*` then has error `< p^6 exp(-p^2)` and bandwidth `< p^{28}`.

| Exponent | Verdict |
| --- | --- |
| 12, 26, 28 | sufficient, and still smallest |
| 6, the normalizer | sufficient, and still smallest |
| 5, 11, 25, 27 | fail, at `p=2` or for `p≥3` at `W=p-1` |

The across-cell bound is the reading of LOG-A’s “downward Gaussian entries”, downstream’s “downward dyadic approximation of the original entry”, and the review’s downward dyadic entries. FINE-PRIME says “rounded” in that place and does not contain the downward phrase. At `p=2`, an overshoot of one part in 64 already exceeds the ceiling, because `63·63=3969>3968=62·64`. A step `g=2` at `θ=β=1/4` makes the bare kernel `exp(-a ρ h^2)` larger than `n` (square gaps 32 and 20 in sixteenths), so downward-of-`Ghat` is a different rule.

**Claim type:** conditional transfer for that banded reference. **No new κ.**

## Not claimed

The four-ulp repair is stated for weights and truncated Toeplitz coefficients. This package does not prove a stored across-cell value lands in `[0, n]`. The ideal `1/(8p^2)` gaps stay the eventual statements in GAUSSIAN and #4402. The Schur complement, the core exponent 400, and the written notes are untouched.

## Test plan

```sh
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/gaussian-cross-exponents
```
